title: Choose what Helm can recover after an upgrade fails
description: Select upgrade flags and inject a failure. Compare Helm release state, Kubernetes resources, and external data instead of treating rollback as one atomic system transaction.

strategies.label: Plain upgrade
strategies.detail: Apply and return without waiting for workload readiness.

strategies.label: Upgrade with --wait
strategies.detail: Wait for supported resources, but do not automatically roll back a failed revision.

strategies.label: Upgrade with --atomic
strategies.detail: Wait and roll back release-managed changes when the upgrade fails.

failures.label: Deployment never becomes Ready
failures.detail: The new Pods fail their readiness checks.

plain.nextStep: Observe rollout health and recover explicitly; the client returned before readiness.

wait.nextStep: Repair or invoke a deliberate rollback after inspecting the failed revision.

atomic.nextStep: Verify the restored workload and investigate why readiness failed.

failures.label: Pre-upgrade hook Job fails
failures.detail: A blocking hook exits unsuccessfully before normal resources update.

plain.nextStep: Inspect hook logs and cleanup policy before retrying.

wait.nextStep: Inspect the hook; --wait does not turn hook code into an idempotent operation.

atomic.nextStep: Confirm hook resources were cleaned according to their explicit deletion policy.

failures.label: External schema migration commits, then Pods fail
failures.detail: A hook changes a database outside the release-managed resource set.

plain.nextStep: Use the database recovery plan; Helm cannot reverse the committed schema change.

wait.nextStep: Recover application and data compatibility before retry or rollback.

atomic.nextStep: The old workload must be forward-compatible with the new schema, or data recovery is required.
